title: Russian missile and drone strikes leave most of Ukraine without power in November 2022
body:
On 23 November 2022 Russian missiles and drones hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure in one of the heaviest attacks of the autumn campaign against the power grid. Ukraine said about 70 cruise missiles and drones were used, killing 10 people and wounding around 50. Al Jazeera reported on 24 November that nearly 80 percent of the country was left without electricity. A new round of strikes the next day killed at least four people in Kherson. Three Ukrainian nuclear plants were disconnected from the grid and were reconnected by Thursday morning, according to the energy ministry, and blackouts also hit neighbouring Moldova.

By Thursday evening Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said 60 percent of homes in the city still had emergency outages. The mayor of Kharkiv, Ihor Terekhov, said power and water were being restored there. The World Health Organization warned of life-threatening consequences and possible mass displacement, and Ukraine's central bank warned that outages could disrupt banking operations.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the attacks a crime against humanity. The US ambassador to the UN, Linda Thomas-Greenfield, said Russia was weaponising winter, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Ukraine could end the suffering by meeting Russia's demands. Russia's defence ministry denied striking anywhere in Kyiv. The strikes were part of a campaign against energy infrastructure that began in October 2022 and continued through the winter.
